QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_31

question.text: The Dissolution Period of a Cat III AIF scheme:

answer.text: Can be extended indefinitely upon investor consent
Shall not be more than the original tenure of the scheme, and cannot be extended after expiry
Is permitted only if SEBI individually approves each case

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 13.7: the Dissolution Period shall NOT be more than the ORIGINAL tenure of the scheme AND shall NOT be extended in any manner upon expiry. A filing via merchant-banker (Information Memorandum + Due-Diligence Certificate) must be made before Liquidation Period expires. **The Trap:** Indefinite extension (A) contradicts the rule. Fixed 2 years (C) is not the rule. SEBI per-case approval (D) misreads the process. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C/D cover the same Dissolution Period cap. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Track the original-tenure clock rigorously — a 6-year scheme had a 6-year Dissolution Period maximum, not open-ended. Fresh commitments and new investments are BARRED during the Dissolution Period.
